## Summary

AMMX is the 68080's 64-bit SIMD unit: a line-F coprocessor with id 7, 3-operand, using D0–D7, E0–E23, A0–A7 and B0–B7, without changing the condition codes.

## Details

- Ammx stands for Apollo MultiMedia eXtension. It is an integrated coprocessor with id=7. It handles 64 bit instructions.
- It has access to 32 64bit wide data registers, D0..7 & E0..23. The same as the integer unit can use. The data can be a multiple bytes or words that are processed in one go. So called Single Instruction Multiple Data or SIMD.
- This division of 64bits into lets say 2 x 32 or 8 x 8 parts is called vector.
- Ammx instructions are normally 3 operand, unlike the 2 operand 68k.
- It can use all the address registers, A0..7 & B0..7.
- Ammx does not change the condition-codes at all. Pcmp sets the condition in the destination register. Bsel can be used to make conditional changes with that.
- See page 56 of the original ([ammx/pcmpccb.md](ammx/pcmpccb.md)) for this example with register values.

```asm
    pcmpgtb	d0,d1,d2	; d2 = (d1>d0)
    bsel		d1,d2,e0	; if (d1>d0) then replace e0 with d1
```

- or storeilm d1,d2,(a0) ; if (d1&lt;=d0) then write d1
- Ammx format: page 42 of the original ([ammx/ammx-format.md](ammx/ammx-format.md))

### Vector handling by type

Which element type each instruction uses, source or destination match. The original shows each list next to its heading.

| Vector type | Instructions |
|---|---|
| Vector Bit (64x bit) | bsel, minterm, pand, pandn, peor, por |
| Vector Byte (8x byte) | bfly, c2p, packuswb, padd, pavg, pcmpccb, pmaxb, pminb, psub, storec, storeilm, storem, storem3, vperm |
| Vector Word (4x word) | bfly, pack3216, packuswb, padd, pcmpccw, pmaxw, pminw, pmul88, pmulh, pmull, psub, storem3, trans, unpack1632 |
| Vector Long (2x long) | pack3216, pmula, storem3, unpack1632 |
| Vector Quad (1 quad) | c2p, load, loadi, lsdq, store, storec, storei, storeilm, storem, storem3, vperm |

- Note: tex & rex are not vector operations.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no SIMD unit. AMMX instructions do not change the condition codes; PCMPcc writes its result to a register.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T branch on condition codes after AMMX instructions: use PCMPcc with BSEL, PAND/PANDN or STOREILM.
